paragraphs: Decision center: the work of earth drillers, except oil and gas, is to turn these front-end conditions — geological and drilling task requirements, site and access and water and power conditions, drilling rigs and drilling tools and well completion equipment, and geotechnical and groundwater information and safety and environmental conditions — into a borehole result with an accurate position, controllable depth and verticality, usable cores and samples, and a usable well, all within safety and environmental boundaries: first determine the hole position, depth, diameter, and coring or well completion requirements according to the task, then mobilize and level and stabilize the site and install and level the drilling rig, then select the rig, bits, and drill rods according to the geotechnical conditions and control rotation speed, air pressure, and down pressure for drilling, during which flush the hole and blow out dust and verify the hole depth and position and verticality, observe the returns, and record the strata, then take cores and samples and log and submit them for testing, and for well completion install the well casing and screen and gravel pack and sealing and wash the well and conduct pumping tests and disinfection, and finally dismantle the rig and restore the site and report anomalies. The point of judgment is not 'can the hole be drilled down' but whether every step of the chain — task and site, positioning and drilling, sampling and well completion, and records and safety — is accurate, verifiable, and handled according to the task and safety and environmental requirements.

Suitable for a first try: willing to stand and operate for long periods in the field and at construction sites under noise, dust, vibration, and weather conditions; able to select drilling tools according to the task and geotechnical conditions and control drilling speed and air pressure and down pressure per the procedures and stay careful about hole depth and position and verticality; able to withstand carrying drill rods and tools and field work and irregular hours; willing to do sampling logging and record keeping and safety and environmental handling and to accept a schedule driven by the project and weather.

Needs caution: if you expect this job to be indoors or to involve only pressing buttons and watching gauges, or you are unwilling to wear protective equipment and follow edge, electrical, hoisting, rotating part, high-pressure line, dust, noise, and wellhead safety requirements (drilling without a stable site or warning barriers, touching rotating parts and high-pressure lines without protective gear, not adjusting drilling speed and air pressure according to the geotechnical conditions, not handling in-hole accidents and dropped tools per the procedures, not disposing of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil as required), or you find it hard to keep precision and patience under repetitive operations and long field hours and abnormal in-hole pressure, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: using the fictional task sheets, hole positions, strata, and drilling tool records provided on this page, complete a paper exercise that 'arranges the hole position, depth, diameter, coring or well completion, and drilling tool selection sequence according to the task — writes a paragraph on drilling speed and air pressure and down pressure and flushing according to the geotechnical conditions — and fills in one hole depth and position and verticality and sampling logging and anomaly and safety record', only to verify whether you are willing to check item by item according to the task and procedures and to record truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials and does not involve real drilling rigs, in-hole operations, blasting, or wellhead equipment, and it does not constitute a geological or engineering or environmental or safety conclusion, nor is it equivalent to job training or a special operation or field work qualification.

Adjacent positions have different duties — rotary drill operators, oil and gas (47-5012.00) handle oil and gas well drilling operations; derrick operators (47-5011.00) handle derrick and drilling tool and wellhead equipment operation and well control; service unit operators (47-5013.00) handle oil and gas well service and workover equipment operation; pile driver operators (47-2072.00) handle pile driving and pile sinking; operating engineers and other construction equipment operators (47-2073.00) handle earthmoving, lifting, and paving construction machinery; construction laborers (47-2061.00) handle general site labor. This occupation is set on operating rotary, cable-tool, and pneumatic drills to extract groundwater and salt deposits, to collect core samples in mineral exploration or soil testing, and to serve blasting operations in mining or construction, including horizontal boring machine and earth boring machine operators. Geology and engineering design and blasting operations and well condition safety and environmental compliance and special operation qualifications are governed by the regulations and standards and competent authorities of the relevant jurisdiction and this project's requirements, are not inferred from the job title, and must not exceed authorization to issue geological or engineering or environmental or safety conclusions externally.

Inputs that must be verified: the task sheet and hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements, site and access and water and power and working face and slope and underground pipeline and buried object conditions, the specifications and inspection and maintenance status of drilling rigs and tools and bits and rods, geotechnical and groundwater and strata information and known cavities and karst and contamination, mud or flushing and dust removal and waste residue and waste oil and wastewater disposal and environmental requirements, edge and electrical and hoisting and rotating part and high-pressure line safety conditions, and sampling logging and progress and safety and environmental record requirements. Things that must not be done: entering and positioning without verifying pipelines and buried objects and slopes and site bearing capacity, drilling without leveling and stabilizing outriggers and setting warning barriers, touching rotating parts and high-pressure lines and transmission parts without protective gear or without shutting down the machine, not selecting bits and adjusting drilling speed and air pressure and down pressure according to the geotechnical conditions, not handling in-hole accidents and dropped tools and stuck pipe and water inflow per the procedures, not disposing of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil as required, and concealing or delaying reports of in-hole anomalies and equipment hazards and safety and environmental problems.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can stand and operate for long periods in the field and at construction sites under noise and dust and vibration and weather conditions, whether you can select drilling tools according to the task and geotechnical conditions and control drilling per the procedures and stay careful about hole depth and position and verticality, whether you can withstand carrying tools and field work and irregular hours, whether you can do sampling logging and record keeping and safety and environmental handling, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization and geological and engineering and safety and environmental boundaries; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of being 'strong' or 'able to drive'; all of this must be confirmed in supervised field work and team observation.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real drilling operations and in-hole operations and blasting and wellhead and electrical and field work must be undertaken by organizations and personnel with the corresponding training and qualifications that follow the regulations and standards of the relevant jurisdiction and this project's requirements; individuals must not exceed authorization to issue geological, engineering, environmental, safety, or compliance conclusions externally, and this page does not constitute geological, engineering, environmental, safety, or legal advice.

The work object of this occupation is the field and construction site: the task sheet and hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements, site and access and water and power and working face and slope and underground pipeline and buried object conditions, the specifications and status of drilling rigs and tools and bits and rods and well completion equipment, geotechnical and groundwater and strata information, mud or flushing and dust removal and waste residue and waste oil and wastewater disposal and environmental requirements, and sampling logging and progress and safety and environmental records. The output is a borehole and well completion result and records that meet the task and depth and verticality requirements: hole position, depth, and diameter completed by specification and geotechnical conditions, cores and samples and logs obtained per the task, well casing and screen and gravel pack and sealing and well washing and pumping tests completed per the design, and verifiable sampling and progress and anomaly and safety and environmental records. The basis for judgment is the task sheet and geological data and geotechnical conditions and drilling rig and tool and safety and environmental procedures, not personal habits or the job title.

Judgment one: whether the task and hole position and depth and diameter are verified clearly — checking the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements against the task sheet and geological data and site conditions, rather than starting to drill from impression.

Judgment two: whether the site and pipelines and buried objects and slopes are safe — confirming site bearing capacity and leveling and outrigger stability and overhead lines and underground pipelines and buried objects and slopes and edge conditions, rather than positioning without checking.

Judgment three: whether drilling tool and bit selection and drilling parameters follow the basis — selecting the rig, bits, and rods according to the geotechnical and strata conditions and controlling rotation speed and air pressure and down pressure and flushing, rather than drilling arbitrarily.

Judgment four: whether hole depth and position and verticality and cores and samples are in place — verifying the hole depth and position and verticality and taking cores and samples and logging and submitting them for testing as required, rather than recording carelessly.

Judgment five: whether well completion and well washing and pumping tests and records are held — installing the well casing and screen and gravel pack and sealing and washing the well and conducting pumping tests and disinfection per the design and recording them, rather than skipping operations.

Judgment six: whether safety and environmental protection and anomalies and handover are held — working per the edge and electrical and hoisting and rotating part and high-pressure line and dust and noise requirements and disposing of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil per the procedures and reporting and handing over per the system when in-hole anomalies or equipment hazards occur, rather than concealing or delaying.

The work of earth drillers, except oil and gas, can be divided into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is task and site and positioning and preparation: study the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements from the task sheet and geological data, survey the site and access and water and power and working face and verify overhead lines and underground pipelines and buried objects and slopes and edge conditions, level and stabilize the site and position and level the truck-mounted or trailer-mounted rig and stabilize the outriggers and extend the mast, assemble and inspect the rig and tools and bits and rods and well completion equipment, and confirm the mud or flushing and dust removal and waste residue and waste oil and wastewater disposal plan and protective equipment and warning measures. The second is drilling and sampling and well completion: select bits and rods according to the geotechnical and strata conditions and operate to control and stabilize the machine and align the tools and start, stop, and adjust drilling, adjust air pressure and rotation speed and down pressure according to the rock or concrete type and add or remove rods and change bits, operate equipment to flush cuttings or blow out dust from the hole, verify the hole position and depth and verticality and align the drilling position, observe returns and changes in drilling speed and record the geological horizons and drilling progress by stratum, take cores and samples and check the cores and submit them for testing, drill for blasting or grouting or anchoring or foundations, and for well completion install the well casing and screen and filter material and sealing and install the pump and other in-well facilities and flush and wash and disinfect and conduct pumping tests, perform routine maintenance and upgrade equipment (replacing parts, hardfacing bits, lubricating machinery), and fish out dropped equipment. The third is records and safety and environmental protection and handover: record the geological horizons and drilling progress and samples and equipment maintenance and in-hole anomalies, dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil per the procedures and restore the site, inspect the protection and warning and electrical and hoisting and rotating part and high-pressure line conditions, and hand over with the team leader and geology and inspection and the back office. All three work surfaces proceed within the task sheet and geological data and geotechnical conditions and drilling rig and tool and safety and environmental procedures.

Core purpose

Turn the task and site and geotechnical conditions and equipment into a borehole result that meets the hole position and depth and verticality and coring or well completion requirements: task and hole position clear, site and pipelines and slopes safe, drilling tools and parameters on a documented basis, sampling and well completion and records in place, and safety and environmental requirements held.

This occupation bears execution responsibility for selecting drilling tools and controlling drilling according to the task and geotechnical conditions and for coring and sampling and casing installation and well completion and records; responsibility for geology and engineering design and blasting operations and well condition safety and environmental acceptance and acceptance is borne by the owner and design unit and construction unit and competent authorities and personnel with the corresponding qualifications according to regulations and standards.

Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with the team leader and geology and surveying and inspection and the back office and equipment repair and safety and environmental personnel, and adjust priorities according to the task and hole depth and schedule and sampling milestones; immediately report in-hole anomalies and equipment hazards and safety and environmental problems and matters beyond authorization.

Conclusion boundaries

Do not enter and position without verifying pipelines and buried objects and slopes and site bearing capacity, do not drill without leveling and stabilizing outriggers and setting warning barriers, do not touch rotating parts and high-pressure lines and transmission parts without protective gear or without shutting down the machine, do not select bits and adjust parameters without regard to the geotechnical conditions, do not fail to handle in-hole accidents and dropped tools and stuck pipe and water inflow per the procedures, do not fail to dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil as required, do not conceal or delay reporting in-hole anomalies and equipment hazards and safety and environmental problems, and do not issue geological or engineering or environmental or safety or compliance conclusions externally beyond authorization.

paragraphs: Rotary drill operators, oil and gas (47-5012.00)

Operate oil and gas rotary drilling rigs according to the design and well control requirements and manage drilling fluid and casing running and cementing, responsible for oil and gas well drilling and well control safety.

The object and procedures differ: rotary drill operators, oil and gas focus on oil and gas wells and drilling fluid and well control and cementing, following oil and gas drilling and well control procedures and subject to special requirements for well control and hydrogen sulfide and firefighting; this page's occupation focuses on water extraction and salt deposits and exploration coring and construction blasting assistance, following the task sheet and geotechnical conditions and safety and environmental procedures. The equipment is similar but the object and well control and qualification requirements differ and cannot be interchanged by name.

If you want to do oil and gas well drilling and well control, you can choose the rotary drill operator direction and check the well control and special training requirements; if you want to do water extraction and exploration coring and earth boring, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Derrick operators, oil and gas (47-5011.00)

Operate the derrick and drilling tools and wellhead equipment on the drill floor and support well control operations, responsible for wellhead and drilling tool operation and well control coordination safety.

The position and authorization differ: derrick operators handle derrick and drilling tool and wellhead equipment operation on the drilling platform and are subject to well control and platform rules; this page's occupation handles rig positioning and drilling and sampling and well completion in the field and at construction sites, with a different work object and operating environment. Both belong to the drilling chain but the position duties and authorization differ.

If you want to do platform derrick and wellhead work, you can choose the derrick operator direction and check the platform and well control requirements; if you want to do field water extraction and exploration drilling, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Service unit operators, oil and gas (47-5013.00)

The object and deliverable differ: service and workover unit operators focus on oil and gas well service and workover equipment and wellbore operations and complete running and pulling and circulation and cementing and similar operations; this page's occupation focuses on drilling tool selection and drilling and coring and sampling and casing installation and well completion and well washing, with different equipment and processes and wellbore conditions.

If you want to do oil and gas well service and workover, you can choose the service unit operator direction and check the corresponding qualifications; if you want to do water extraction and exploration drilling and well completion, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Pile driver operators (47-2072.00)

The object and process differ: pile driver operators focus on piles and pile sinking and foundations, following pile foundation codes and driving piles into place according to the foundation design; this page's occupation focuses on drilling and coring and well completion according to the task sheet and geotechnical conditions, with different hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements.

If you want to do pile foundations and pile sinking, you can choose the pile driver operator direction; if you want to do water wells and exploration and blasting assistance drilling, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Operating engineers and other construction equipment operators (47-2073.00)

The object and process differ: construction equipment operators focus on earthmoving and excavation and lifting and paving machinery operations; this page's occupation focuses on the rig and drilling tools and drilling and well completion processes, with different equipment and outputs and acceptance basis.

If you want to do earthmoving and lifting and paving, you can choose the construction equipment operator direction; if you want to do drilling and well completion, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Construction laborers (47-2061.00)

The duties and process differ: construction laborers focus on on-site carrying and cleaning and auxiliary work and do not take on rig operation and sampling and well completion duties; this page's occupation focuses on rig operation and drilling and coring and sampling and well completion and requires separate verification of special operation and safety qualification requirements.

If you want to do general on-site labor, you can choose the construction laborer direction; if you want to operate a rig and complete drilling and well completion, this page's occupation is more suitable.

Observation signal two: willing to follow edge and electrical and hoisting and rotating part and high-pressure line and dust and noise safety and environmental procedures, and to confirm before acting where in-hole and equipment and safety and environmental matters are involved.

entries.answer: This page's occupation operates rotary, cable-tool, and pneumatic drills in the field according to the task to extract groundwater and salt and to take cores and samples in exploration or soil testing and to drill for construction and mining blasting assistance; rotary drill operators and derrick operators handle oil and gas well drilling and well control; pile driver operators handle piles and pile sinking and foundations. outlook_evidence.value: The U.S. O*NET new-hire education feedback is high school/equivalent 73%, less than high school 15%, and postsecondary certificate 12%; Job Zone1—2/SVP<6 is a group preparation description with several days to 1 year of training, not a legal threshold for this occupation or that everyone learns it in a few weeks. BLS2025 exact line typically requires high school, less than 5 years of related experience, and long-term on-the-job training; the two sets of indicators differ, so the group label cannot be used to claim that zero experience is always hired or that short training is universal. Order No. 35 as amended by Order No. 78 applies to geological exploration of metal and non-metal minerals and does not apply to exploration in producing mines; Article 7 requires a safety permit for drilling and trenching construction units within that scope, Article 8 requires written reports, Article 9 covers systems, and Articles 18/19 cover protection, rescue, and emergency response. Article 11 requires special personnel to receive dedicated training, assessment, and the corresponding certificate; Article 12 requires trenching personnel to receive at least 72h initially and 20h of annual retraining, and this is not extended to all surface drillers. Article 15 requires a special safety chapter and review for trenching design, and this is not extended to general water wells or all earth boring. The 2017 geological exploration qualification approval has been cancelled, and a 2025 public reply from the Ministry of Natural Resources confirms that solid mineral exploration units and personnel have no such access threshold; the old 'qualification certificate' can no longer be listed as a current general condition, and this does not exempt safety permits or special operation certification. The current reporting materials, competent authorities, and local processing are verified separately.

description.text: Earth drillers, except oil and gas (O*NET-SOC 47-5023.00) operate rotary, cable-tool, and pneumatic drills in the field and at construction sites: they study the task sheet and geological data and survey the site and pipelines and slopes, position and level the rig and stabilize the outriggers, select drilling tools according to the geotechnical conditions and control rotation speed and air pressure and down pressure and flushing, verify hole depth and position and verticality and take cores and samples and log and submit for testing, install well casing and screen and filter material and sealing and wash the well and conduct pumping tests and disinfection, drill for blasting and grouting and anchoring and foundations, perform routine maintenance and upgrade equipment and dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil and restore the site. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 60,190 USD per year (28.94 USD per hour), with annual percentiles of 44,460 / 49,900 / 60,190 / 72,450 / 83,800 USD; 2024 employment was about 18,300, and the 2024—2034 projection is 'average (3% to 4%)' with about 1,700 projected openings; the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 and the interest code is RCI. Mainland China: geological exploration units carrying out drilling and trenching construction should obtain a work safety license under the Interim Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Work Safety in Geological Exploration of Metal and Non-metal Mineral Resources and submit a written report, and special operation personnel must hold a special operation certificate to take the post; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage definition, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.summary: Earth drillers, except oil and gas (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 47-5023.00, Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas) are drilling operation positions in the field and at construction sites: they operate various rigs such as rotary, cable-tool, and pneumatic drills to extract groundwater and salt deposits, collect core samples in mineral exploration or soil testing, and facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction (including horizontal boring machine and earth boring machine operators); the work includes studying the task sheet and geological data to determine the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements, surveying the site and pipelines and slopes and positioning and leveling the rig and stabilizing the outriggers and extending the mast, assembling and inspecting the drilling tools and bits and rods and well completion equipment, selecting bits and rods according to the geotechnical and strata conditions and controlling rotation speed and air pressure and down pressure and flushing, adding or removing rods and changing bits and verifying hole position and depth and verticality, observing returns and recording strata and coring and sampling and logging and submitting for testing, installing well casing and screen and filter material and sealing and installing pumps when completing wells and washing and disinfecting and conducting pumping tests, drilling for blasting and grouting and anchoring and foundations, performing routine maintenance and upgrading equipment and fishing out dropped equipment, disposing of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil per the procedures and restoring the site and reporting and handing over when anomalies occur. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 60,190 USD per year (28.94 USD per hour), with annual percentiles of 44,460 / 49,900 / 60,190 / 72,450 / 83,800 USD (hourly percentiles 21.37 / 23.99 / 28.94 / 34.83 / 40.29); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 18,300, a 2024—2034 projection of 'average (Average, 3% to 4%)', and about 1,700 projected job openings (that source gives only the category and range rather than a single precise percentage, and this page follows the source wording); the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), the education feedback is 73% high school or equivalent and 15% less than high school graduation and 12% postsecondary certificate, the interest code is RCI, and there are 29 tasks; the work context includes face-to-face discussions every day 75%, continuous contact with others 39%, telephone every day 35%, teamwork 'extremely important' 34%, decision freedom 'very large' 66%, precision or accuracy 'extremely important' 16% + 'very important' 50%, standing continuously or almost continuously 52%, exposure to hazardous equipment every day 71%, wearing common protective or safety equipment every day 84%, noise every day 65%, extreme heat or extreme cold every day 28% + weekly or more 39%, outdoor all kinds of weather every day 79%, whole-body vibration every day 42% + weekly or more 43%, repeating the same tasks 'extremely important' 18%, consequences of error 'extremely serious' 52%, competition 'no competition' 33%, making decisions every day 44%, and time pressure every day 20%. Mainland China definition: geological exploration units carrying out drilling and trenching construction should obtain a work safety license under the Interim Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Work Safety in Geological Exploration of Metal and Non-metal Mineral Resources (promulgated by the State Administration of Work Safety Order No. 35 and amended by Order No. 78) and, holding a geological exploration qualification certificate and project task approval document or contract, submit a written report to the county-level work safety supervision and administration department where the work area is located, and should establish systems for work safety responsibility and position operating procedures and education and training and hidden danger investigation and treatment and emergency response; special operation personnel must undergo dedicated safety technical training and pass the assessment and obtain a special operation certificate before taking the post; trenching workers should receive at least 72 hours of work safety education before first taking the post and at least 20 hours of retraining each year thereafter; the design and construction and safety management of geological exploration engineering should comply with the Safety Code for Geological Exploration (AQ 2004); the trenching engineering design plan should include a special safety chapter and be reviewed and approved. The above is cited by regulation and standard name and verified key points, and article numbers were not verified one by one. This occupation has no unified access-type occupational qualification in mainland China. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage definition corresponding to this occupation, this page preserves the gap as it stands, and industry average wages serve only as a visible industry proxy.
